stories.title: Only 2.5% of Recent Bitcoin Buyers Are in Profit on Exchange Deposits
stories.summary: On-chain data shows that just 2.5% of Bitcoin sent to exchanges by recent buyers sits in profit, CryptoSlate reported. The figure points to heavy unrealized losses among buyers who bought near recent highs. The report gave no further breakdown of the data.
stories.whyItMatters: A low profit ratio among recent buyers can signal capitulation risk or a market bottom, so traders watch this metric closely.
whatToWatch: Whether the profit ratio recovers as price moves
Signs of forced selling from underwater holders
questions: What price level would return these buyers to profit?
Does the data cover new coins only, or recycled supply too?

sources.title: Just 2.5% of recent Bitcoin buyers’ exchange deposits were in profit

stories.title: Fluidkey Hack Drains $1.6 Million Despite Keys Staying on Users' Devices
stories.summary: Fluidkey suffered a $1.6 million hack, CryptoSlate reported. The breach happened even though the service keeps private keys on users' own devices. The incident points to a security gap that sits outside key custody itself.
stories.whyItMatters: The hack is a reminder that self-custody design alone does not remove every attack surface, a point users and regulators weigh when they judge wallet safety claims.
whatToWatch: Fluidkey's response and any plan to compensate affected users
Further detail on the exact vulnerability exploited
questions: What part of the system did the attacker actually exploit?
Do other wallets with similar architecture carry the same risk?

sources.title: Fluidkey’s $1.6 million hack exposes a security risk even when private keys never leave users’ devices

stories.title: Variational's $1.5 Billion Trading Business Has a Catch for Profitable Traders
stories.summary: Variational runs a trading business tied to $1.5 billion in activity, CryptoSlate reported. The report says even traders who turn a profit face a catch built into the platform. The report did not spell out what the catch is.
stories.whyItMatters: Readers who use newer trading venues need to know about fee structures or mechanics that can offset gains, even on a winning trade.
whatToWatch: Further reporting that explains the specific catch
Any response from traders who use the platform
questions: What exactly is the catch that profitable traders face?
How does it compare to costs on established exchanges?

sources.title: Variational’s $1.5 billion trading business has a catch even profitable traders cannot escape

stories.title: Bitcoin ETF Investors Get a Way to Hedge Thanksgiving's Long Trading Gap
stories.summary: US stock markets close for more than 40 hours around Thanksgiving, so Bitcoin ETF holders cannot trade shares even though Bitcoin itself keeps trading. CryptoSlate reported that investors have a way to hedge this gap. The gap creates a window where the ETF price cannot react to crypto market moves.
stories.whyItMatters: The holiday gap is a known risk for ETF holders, since Bitcoin can swing sharply while they cannot exit or adjust positions.
whatToWatch: Bitcoin price action over the Thanksgiving holiday
Trading volume and price gaps when US markets reopen
questions: What specific instrument are investors using to hedge?
How many holders actually hedge versus simply holding through the gap?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETF investors have a way to hedge during Thanksgiving’s 40+ hour trading gap

stories.title: Sky's Nearly 30% Yield Comes With a Near-Frozen Lending Vault
stories.summary: The Sky protocol advertises a yield near 30%, but CryptoSlate reported that 99.96% of its lending vault is not available for immediate withdrawal. Almost all deposited funds sit locked in some form, despite the headline rate. That gap between advertised yield and withdrawable funds is a liquidity risk for depositors.
stories.whyItMatters: High DeFi yields often hide liquidity constraints, and this is a concrete case for readers to weigh before they chase a headline rate.
whatToWatch: Whether Sky changes vault liquidity or withdrawal terms
Any sign of depositor complaints or a run on the vault
questions: What causes almost all of the vault to be locked?
Is this liquidity limit disclosed clearly before depositors commit funds?

sources.title: Sky offers nearly 30% yield but 99.96% of its lending vault is unavailable for immediate withdrawals

stories.title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Set to Jump 8.5%, Squeezing Miner Profitability
stories.summary: Bitcoin's mining difficulty is headed for a rise of about 8.5%, CryptoSlate reported. A higher difficulty means miners need more computing power to earn the same reward, which cuts into margins. The adjustment adds pressure on miners that already run on thin profitability.
stories.whyItMatters: Rising difficulty can push less efficient miners offline or toward consolidation, which affects network hash rate and security over time.
whatToWatch: The actual difficulty adjustment once it locks in
Miner hash rate changes and any capacity shutdowns
questions: Which miners sit closest to the margin where this hurts most?
Is the difficulty rise driven by more hash rate or by faster block times?

sources.title: Bitcoin miners face a new profitability cliff as difficulty heads for an 8.5% jump

stories.title: DBS Builds Two Routes to 24/7 Dollar Settlement With JPMorgan and Circle
stories.summary: Singapore's DBS Bank is building two separate paths for round-the-clock dollar transfers, CryptoSlate reported. One route works with JPMorgan, and the other uses Circle's USDC stablecoin. The move is part of a wider push by banks to offer always-on settlement.
stories.whyItMatters: A major bank building stablecoin rails alongside bank-to-bank rails shows institutional finance is putting real infrastructure behind crypto assets, not just watching from the sidelines.
whatToWatch: The rollout timeline for each route
Which clients or use cases get access first
questions: How do the JPMorgan and Circle routes differ in practice?
Will other banks follow with similar dual-rail setups?

sources.title: DBS is building two paths for 24/7 dollars with JPMorgan and Circle using USDC

stories.title: Binance Raises RLUSD Yield to 6.37% as XRP Reward Payouts Jump 54%
stories.summary: Binance raised the yield on its RLUSD stablecoin product to 6.37%, CryptoSlate reported. At the same time, rewards paid out in XRP rose by 54%. Both moves are part of Binance's ongoing yield promotions on its platform.
stories.whyItMatters: Exchange yield rates shift often and show how platforms compete for deposits, but readers should treat promotional rates as temporary, not fixed income.
whatToWatch: Whether the 6.37% rate holds or is a limited-time promotion
Changes to other stablecoin or token yields on Binance
questions: How long will Binance keep this rate in place?
What funds the increase in XRP rewards?

sources.title: Binance raises RLUSD yield to 6.37% as XRP rewards surge 54%

stories.title: Meta's AI Agents Ran 1,000+ Experiments in a Month for a 0.23% Search Gain
stories.summary: Meta's AI agents ran more than 1,000 experiments in a single month, CryptoSlate reported. The effort improved search performance by just 0.23%. The result shows a large gap between the volume of automated experiments and the size of the measured gain.
stories.whyItMatters: This story sits outside crypto markets directly, but it is a data point on how much automated AI research effort actually pays off, a question that also feeds AI-linked token narratives.
whatToWatch: Whether Meta scales up or pulls back this experimentation approach
Follow-up results in later reporting periods
questions: Why did such a high volume of experiments yield such a small gain?
Does this change how Meta allocates its AI research resources?

sources.title: Meta’s AI agents ran over 1,000 experiments in a month but improved search by just 0.23%

stories.title: HSBC Lets Hong Kong Customers Buy a Money-Market Fund With HK$100 via RedCoin
stories.summary: HSBC now lets customers in Hong Kong buy into a money-market fund starting at HK$100, using a token called RedCoin, CryptoSlate reported. The low minimum opens fund access to smaller retail investors. The move is part of a wider bank push into tokenized financial products.
stories.whyItMatters: A major bank lowering the entry point for tokenized fund access shows traditional finance keeps building retail-facing uses for blockchain-based settlement.
whatToWatch: Uptake among Hong Kong retail customers
Whether HSBC expands RedCoin to other products or markets
questions: What backs or governs RedCoin as a token?
Will other banks in the region offer similar low-minimum tokenized products?

sources.title: HSBC lets Hong Kong customers buy a money-market fund with HK$100 in RedCoin
